column3: Notes: Mid-range centric better OG EJ07 with the best vocals I've heard so far - comes with "free" custom fit/shell if you want. Insane staging super wide, scales great, even more immersive than OG EJ07s. Makes you ascend and lose track of time.. Sound: mid-centric. Strengths: great vocals, scales with volume. Tuning grade CHINESE KFC EGGTART, tech ?. Value: Worth if you got the $$$

Notes: Pre-Production Unit with a different tuning. A better version of the U12T vocal/tuning wise, no mid scoop and wonkiness. (#1 or #2 vocals for me). Vocals are sweet, extended, open, airy, but also never fatiguing, and naturally weighted. No BA timbre, very natural. Perfect amount of treble detail and air while allowing it to scale at higher volumes. Super smooth dynamics and incredible coherency. TOTL resolution, detail, layering, imaging, and staging. Bass is fine, but not a basshead set - still has a nice slam to it. 07 still scales better and more 3D, but CAD12 stage is more open and better tech. If you don't blast your brains out like me then this is it (although I'm not sure if they're selling this version - maybe request it specifically/ask Joseph?). Strengths: airy treble, natural timbre, detailed, smooth, dynamic/engaging, imaging, separation/layering, bass texture/slam, technical, wide/3D stage, scales with volume. Weaknesses: can be fatiguing. Tuning grade S/S+, tech S. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: TOTL all-rounder with "endgame" tech across the board, a better tuned U12T with better bass texture. Strengths: technical, bass texture/slam, all-rounder. Tuning grade S, tech S. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: TOTL balanced clean tonality with great detail and resolution. ESTs are well implemented - smooth but textured with good air. Could use more low-end and can get slightly bright depending on tips, but bass texture is great. No complaints. Endgame level across the board.. Sound: balanced, bright. Strengths: detailed, airy treble, smooth, bass texture/slam. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S+. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: Retail version has more treble energy and less mid-bass vs pre-production tuning. Very airy and detailed, amazing layering, and one of the most resolving TOTL IEMs along with U12T.. Strengths: airy treble, detailed, separation/layering. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S+. Value: Big Diminishing R
Notes: Musical baby. Tuning grade S/S+, tech S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Vocal benchmark for female vocals under $2000. Clean, airy, sweet, ethereal. Better than Diva and direct upgrade to OG Oracle and OG Mangird Tea. What the Braindamage and Cantor wishes they could be. Great technical performance, and scales decently well. Recommended listening volume is mid to high volume around 75-80dbs. Not for bassy libraries like hiphop, and can be a bit energetic on kpop/jpop/rock stuff with a lot of treble.. Strengths: great vocals, airy treble, technical, scales with volume. Not for: rock, hip-hop, k-pop/j-pop. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Endgame all-rounder tuning around $1000, very close to my all-rounder target. Great balance of detail, dynamics, and refinement - more transients and sharper attack than MK4, but also smoother than the more energetic Glacier. Basically zero issues with endgame performance across the board - maybe more sub-bass? And better scaling on more energetic tracks, but aside from that it's musical, technical, and versatile.. Strengths: all-rounder, detailed, dynamic/engaging, smooth, technical. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble, lacks sub-bass. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Best of the best in most areas, but vocals and mids can be thin due to fit issues. Insane bass texture/detail and HUGE soundstage. One of the best trebles I've heard.. Strengths: detailed, wide/3D stage, bass texture/slam. Weaknesses: thin, fit issues. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it (on sale)

Notes: Smooth, clean, balanced, and slightly airy in the balance switch. Goes from a clean all-rounder to a warm/bassy all-rounder. Great tech. Basically a cheaper Prestige LTD with more tuning options. "Endgame" for most people, but the case is SHIT.. Sound: balanced, bassy, warm. Strengths: airy treble, smooth, all-rounder, technical. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Clean and natural signature with treble emphasis. LOTS of details with airy treble without going overboard (better treble extension vs MK2/MK3). Bass is not as impactful versus MK3 but has better separation. Overall a technical monster, but can be a bit dry due to less mid-bass. Vocals are further vs MK3 and MK2 (not as forward), giving it that open sense of space. MK2 still the best for vocals, but LTD is an endgame all-rounder.. Sound: bright. Strengths: natural timbre, airy treble, detailed, separation/layering, technical, all-rounder. Weaknesses: dry. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it
Notes: U-shaped/Slight V/W Shaped. Energetic treble. Great tech. Fun signature.. Sound: u-shaped. Strengths: technical, dynamic/engaging. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Sub-bass boost + treble boost. Similar to Crimson, lots of treble energy, great tech, more aggresive LTD.. Sound: bassy, bright. Strengths: technical. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it
Notes: The best basshead set. EXPENSIVE. If you just want bass HBB Punch way better value.. Sound: bassy. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: Super clean and clear sound. Beautiful vocals. Everyhting is extremely well balanced. No special sauce tho.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: great vocals. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: V/W Shaped. Energetic treble. Great tech. Fun bass and engaging signature. Overpriced?. Strengths: technical, dynamic/engaging. Weaknesses: overpriced. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S/S-. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: Neutral tuning with one of the clearest mid-ranges. Natural and clean vocals. Great resolution, separation, and detail. Can be a little dry with its analytical presentation. Bass is well-seperated from other instruments, but nothing special especially at $1K. Would've liked more depth, and treble is also a bit unstable and dips, resulting in a lack of air/depth. Mid-bass is just enough for my library, but would've liked more for genres like hiphop and rock. Cable is heavy, and fit may be too big for many (need to shove in deep).. Sound: neutral. Strengths: great vocals, natural timbre, detailed, separation/layering. Weaknesses: dry, fit issues. Tuning grade S, tech S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Better low-end texture and overall more engaging than MK2, but lacks the mid-range/vocal magic, so depending on your preference either is great. Still TOTL tech like MK2. Great all-rounder.. Strengths: bass texture/slam, dynamic/engaging, technical, all-rounder. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Clean, neutral, and clear vocals. Reminds me of a cleaner Volume S or slightly better OG Oracle, but very expensive, maybe if you can find one around $1000 since it's more of a sidegrade to RSV, Mystic 8, and Arcanis vocal wise. If you want clean vocals Monarch MK2 does the same thing but for $800 less.. Sound: neutral. Strengths: great vocals. Tuning grade S/S-, tech S-. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: Best bassy set under $1K. Bassy/thicker meta tuning. You can actually feel the reverb and vibration from the bone conduction drivers, great control and low-end texture. Mids and treble are also well extended with no major issues, although it can get sharp at times with the snares/electronic stuff ie, past 3:30 on Time by Hikaru Utada.. Sound: bassy. Strengths: bass texture/slam. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble. Not for: edm. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Clean, balanced but engaging sound, clear vocals, great midrange and tech. Vocals can be a bit too forward/sharp. The most recent unit I got sounds different than the earlier ones which was bass-boosted diffuse field.. Sound: balanced, bassy, diffuse-field. Strengths: great vocals, technical, dynamic/engaging. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble. Tuning grade S-, tech S/S-. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: TOTL imaging chops/layering. Tons of micro-details. Great bass texture. Wide and 3D staging. Can be aggressive, and get fatiguing when cranked up/long-listening sessions.. Strengths: imaging, separation/layering, detailed, bass texture/slam, wide/3D stage. Weaknesses: can be fatiguing. Tuning grade S-, tech S/S-. Value: Worth it (on sale)

Notes: A more neutral/slightly warm MEST MK2, less aggresive, easier to the ears, same technicalities. A little overpriced ngl.. Sound: warm, neutral. Weaknesses: overpriced. Tuning grade S-, tech S/S-. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: Best Treble around it's price. Super airy but still smooth. Bass-scoop isn't as bad as I thought, but those who want mid-bass - avoid it.. Strengths: airy treble, smooth. Weaknesses: lacks mid-bass. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: U-shaped, nice treble extention and dynamics, solid vocals, more low-end emphasis than MK3, dynamic and great all-rounder that doesn't specialize in anything.. Sound: u-shaped. Strengths: great vocals, dynamic/engaging, all-rounder. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: Very technical, amazing resolution and detail for the price, treble is slightly crispy and sparkly, clean but dynamic all-rounder. Mid-volume set for the most part as treble can get hot at higher volumes. Easy rec, direct upgrade from Astrals.. Strengths: detailed, technical, dynamic/engaging, all-rounder. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Good Value

Notes: Balanced all-rounder but still dynamic enough, natural timbre, treble is airy, and great tech for the price (around the same as Top Pro). Falls inbetween Hype 4 MK2 and Mega 7 in-terms of energy and dynamics. Cleaner and less bassy vs OG Tea Pro and a bump in detail and also smoother. Similar tuning to Top Pro but less vocal focused/sparkly, and more all-rounded/fuller. Great tech for the price. My unit graphs/sound different (less bass) than HBB's - you've been warned.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: airy treble, technical, natural timbre, dynamic/engaging, all-rounder, smooth, detailed. Weaknesses: unit variance. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Good Value

Notes: Balanced, clean, airy, with a slight treble emphasis, good EST implementation, great overall package and accesories at the price. Similar to TOP PRO but with ESTs and not as vocal centric. Easy rec if you want something balanced and airy.. Sound: bright, balanced. Strengths: airy treble. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Good Value

Notes: Smooth treble, natural timbre, good sub-bass focused set, but transients can be a bit soft, and vocals are pulled back lacking final extension - non-fatiguing but not very engaging and "dynamic". A bassier 5+2 with smoother/more natural treble. Reminds me of the Luna but less mid-bass/vocals, more sub, and a little smoother. Bassy all-rounder like MK4 bass switch but with pulled back vocals, and less versatile since no switch option.. Sound: bassy. Strengths: smooth, natural timbre, dynamic/engaging, all-rounder. Weaknesses: recessed mids/vocals, soft transients. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: Endgame clarity and layering. Clean, clear, and balanced all-rounder sound. Great resolution, and open staging. Rumbly sub-bass but mid-bass tuck can kill some libraries and affect vocal thinness.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: separation/layering, all-rounder, detailed, wide/3D stage, bass texture/slam. Weaknesses: lacks mid-bass. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Disc

Notes: Clean, neutral, balanced, technical, laid back, very detailed. Neutral tuning done right while being a little dynamic/engaging. Tip wise Azla spinfits for more detail, tangzu sancai regular for smoother.. Sound: neutral, balanced. Strengths: detailed, technical, dynamic/engaging. Weaknesses: recessed mids/vocals. Tuning grade S-, tech S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: TOTL tech. Mid-scoop can affect mids/vocal texture and placement, recessed midrange, treble is harsh at high volumes. Great bass detail, but could have more impact.. Strengths: technical, detailed, bass texture/slam. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble, recessed mids/vocals. Tuning grade A+, tech S/S+. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: Great bass texture. BC driver actually works. Very well controlled but still impactful. Great resolution. Doesn't scale well because of spicy uppermids. Vocals often gets shouty on certain tracks, also overpriced asf imo. Strengths: bass texture/slam, detailed. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble, shouty upper mids, overpriced. Tuning grade A+, tech S/S-. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: Very technical bright leaning set, treble air is amazing, very detailed in the treble but also has lots of energy, can get fatiguing - treblehead set?. Sound: bright. Strengths: airy treble, detailed, technical. Weaknesses: can be fatiguing. Tuning grade A, tech S+. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: TOTL mids. Most 3D and holographic staging yet. Imaging, separation, layering, and staging are all S level - only thing that's holding it back is the darker treble which can lead to softer notes vs, Diva, for example.The most immersive set for rock, alternative, ballads, and classical. An 07M that scales better with better staging. Great clarity and seperation. Treble is pushed back but still clear and evident in tracks (at higher volumes). Could use more low-end (but not an issue) and sharper note transients. Takes you on a journey. Needs to be listened to at high volume for the full effect.. Sound: dark. Strengths: wide/3D stage, imaging, separation/layering, scales with volume. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble. Good for: rock, ballads, classical. Tuning grade S+, tech A+. Value: Worth it (High VOL)

Notes: Mid-vol ranking. Clean, mid-range focused, but treble is dark and a bit hard to hear at lower volumes. Needs to be cranked up to hear the details. Imaging, spearation, and staging is top tier, if it weren't for the lower sharpness/not as sparkly, 07 at higher volumes would be an S for tech.. Sound: mid-centric, dark. Strengths: detailed, imaging. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble. Tuning grade A, tech A. Value: Eh

Notes: Check the other RSV ranking below... But that aside, this unit has one of the best vocals I've heard on any IEM (especially for male artists). Mids and Treble is TOTL, smooth and well extended and has great naturalness and the perfect bite. Bass has great speed and still slams (even though it's BA? not rumbly), but stage and detail is average at it's price, but once it clicks with a track it's one of the most beautiful thing ever. Ran into distortion issues at high volume, but may be due to my source? (RSV too sensitive?). Strengths: great vocals, smooth, natural timbre, bass texture/slam, detailed. Tuning grade S/S+, tech A+. Value: 1 of 1 qc pull

Notes: Natural, immersive, full, with special sauce in the staging - decay has a prolonged reverb feeling to the stage/3D like. HIGH VOLUME LISTENING RECOMMENDED. Well-balanced, basically a fuller/thicker OG EJ07 - also reminds me of a sub-bass boosted OG MiM Dark Magician. Build is insanely sturdy and can withstand 4 tons of force on my hydraulic press without getting squashed. Only nitpick is the price since technical performance/micro details/imaging could be better, but I guess they can charge this much since it's the only one with this kind of staging and tonality on the market currently - got a premium tax on it - it is what it is.. Sound: balanced, bassy, dark. Strengths: wide/3D stage, natural timbre, detailed, technical, imaging. Weaknesses: overpriced. Tuning grade S/S+, tech A+. Value: Worth it (but expensive)

Notes: Best Harman IEM under $600 (my unit is less harman), smooth and natural, great layering and tech, bass texture could be better/not as good as Oracle MK3, but overall very balanced and great all-rounder, also, amazing unboxing and accessories. Sound: balanced, harman. Strengths: smooth, technical, separation/layering, bass texture/slam, natural timbre, all-rounder. Weaknesses: unit variance. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: New unit is better tuned/balanced, smooth, good all-rounder, and sounds like adjusted diffusefield.. Sound: balanced, diffuse-field. Strengths: smooth, all-rounder. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Neutral, clean, well-balanced, monitor like, great tech, but boring. Just get the TOP PRO, Oracle MK3 or Volare, or Xuan Wu Gate.. Sound: neutral, balanced. Strengths: technical. Tuning grade A/A+, tech A+. Value: Eh

Notes: Super smoooth. TOTL dynamics and treble air - dunno how they managed this airy and smooth with only BAs. Very clean, no sharpness, or sudden peaks, endgame separation and detail. Only drawback is that the sub-bass is a bit meh, and that the sound isn't that "unique". Very safe all-rounder, and one of the best under $1000. Endgame set. Aside from the bass, everything else is better than Monarch MK3, MK2 still has better vocals, but the Supernova beats them when it comes to treble extention and smootheness - too bad it's impossible to get one lol.. Strengths: airy treble, dynamic/engaging, smooth, detailed, separation/layering, all-rounder. Weaknesses: lacks sub-bass. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Great bass texture, much better than predecessors, smooth and slightly airy giving it a sizzly timbre, great layering/separation, vocals are slightly laid back but not gone, very balanced across frequencies, monitor like, great all-rounder, and pretty safe - although not very dynamic and "fun". Azla clear tips gives a detail boost.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: airy treble, smooth, separation/layering, bass texture/slam, natural timbre, all-rounder, dynamic/engaging, detailed. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble, recessed mids/vocals. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Fast and clean bass but still rumbly and punchy. Beryllium DD baby. Well-seperated mids, and vocals still pop and aren't buried like other bass sets. Can use more treble extension (fixed with AZLA sedna tips).. Strengths: bass texture/slam, separation/layering. Weaknesses: recessed mids/vocals. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Clean, clear, mid-range focused. Beautiful natural, open, and airy female vocals with slight bite to consonants. Reminds me of a fresh ocean breeze. Great vocals, reminds me of a more textured and detailed Oracle MK1. Great separation and layering. Low-end is lean and can get thin and sharp on certain tracks. Great for indie, ballads, acoustics, instrumentals, slower pop/R&B. Doesn't scale good on energetic genres due to the lean low-end and sharper transients - can get peaky on brighter songs. Not recommended for anything that needs low-end like hiphop, rap, rock. Nicher set for vocals.. Sound: mid-centric, lean, bright. Strengths: airy treble, natural timbre, great vocals, detailed, separation/layering. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble, thin. Good for: pop, ballads, acoustic, indie, r&b, instrumentals. Not for: rock, hip-hop. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it (vocals)

Notes: Airy and relaxing vocals. Sweet and gentle presentation. Clean, clear vocals - could be too balanced and tame, could use better transients. Great separation, but stage size could be better.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: airy treble, great vocals, separation/layering. Weaknesses: soft transients. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+. Value: Worth it (vocals)

Notes: Bassy dynamic all-rounder with great low-end texture that slams hard with good note-weight/body. V-shape leaning and slight Hype 4 upgrade. Treble is smooth enouhg while holding dynamics, and vocals are well-tuned. Overall unboxing/accesories are great... just no ESTs at its price, I'd wait for sale.. Sound: bassy, v-shaped. Strengths: bass texture/slam, dynamic/engaging, all-rounder, smooth. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+. Value: Worth it (on sale)

Notes: Clean, clear, smooth with airy treble emphasis/has the sauce, OCD pin point imaging, amazing detail retrieval and separation - punches way above its price point tech wise. Only downside is that treble can be too much on energetic genres like kpop/jpop/edm, and mid-bass could use more engagement for rock/bands - not a bassy set. Doesn't scale well, a mid-volume set that excels with certain genres like indie, acoustics, ballads, r&b, and slower pop stuff - recommended library playlist: https://music.apple.com/ca/playlist/hype-4-mk2/pl.u-55D6PmKiMZqGb9. Sound: bright. Strengths: airy treble, smooth, detailed, imaging, separation/layering, technical. Good for: pop, ballads, acoustic, indie, r&b. Not for: rock, k-pop/j-pop, edm. Tuning grade A+, tech S/S-. Value: GREAT Value... BUT

Notes: Bright lean "Meta" inspired all-rounder, well-balanced, smooth, with great transients, and basically a slightly more detailed Astral with smoother treble and less sub-bass.Great details and tech for the price.. Sound: bright, balanced, lean. Strengths: smooth, detailed, technical, all-rounder. Weaknesses: lacks sub-bass. Tuning grade S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Clean, natural, balanced, but also still engaging and musical. Timbre is very realistic and treble is smooth enough while giving enough transients. Can get sharp at higher volumes. If you're looking for a chopin/daybreak upgrade these are it.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: natural timbre, dynamic/engaging, smooth. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble. Tuning grade S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Balanced, smooth, and clean presentation that scales beautifully with slightly forward/powerful vocals.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: smooth, scales with volume. Tuning grade S-, tech A+/S-. Value: Worth it

Notes: Bright leaning set with great tech. Clean mid-range, sharp imaging, sparkly female vocals with decent amount of air. Does get fatiguing and sharp on more energetic tracks and genres like EDM/POP/KPOP/JPOP, aka lower to mid volume set. Sounds very good on slower genres like indie, acoustics, ballads - adds more energy and liveliness to the slower nature of those genres. Mid-bass is lacking and would not recommend for rock or hiphop.. Sound: bright. Strengths: technical, airy treble, imaging. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble, can be fatiguing, lacks mid-bass. Good for: ballads, acoustic, indie. Not for: k-pop/j-pop, edm, pop, rock, hip-hop. Tuning grade A+/S-, tech S-. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: Clean, clear, neutral-vocal leaning tuning with basically no low-end. Great layering, separation, imaging, and detail... however vocals can sound thin and too light due to the rolled off bass, and if you need low-end - forget it. Very niche iem for instrumentals or vocal ballads that has no low-end elements. Also costs way too much, and the unboxing is lowkey a scam at that price. Both the Perseus and CKLVX would be better value wise.. Sound: neutral, lean. Strengths: detailed, imaging, separation/layering. Weaknesses: thin, overpriced. Tuning grade A/A+, tech S/S-. Value: Big Diminishing R

Notes: My favourite vocals under $500 (best imo). A more refined OG Mangird Tea with better resolution and tech. Has the "sauce" in the treble with slight bite/sizzle that adds dynamic contrast to vocal consonants. Recommend listening at higher volumes on slower vocal centric tracks. Don't rec hiphop or genres that needs lots of sub-bass. Can get spicy with kpop/jpop at higher volumes/don't rec blasting with more energetic tracks. Pin point imaging and open staging, good for gaming.. Sound: mid-centric. Strengths: detailed, technical, dynamic/engaging, wide/3D stage, imaging. Weaknesses: sharp/harsh treble. Good for: gaming. Not for: hip-hop, k-pop/j-pop. Tuning grade S, tech A+. Value: Worth it (GENRE SPECIFIC)

Notes: Weighted and airy vocals but with expansive staging. 3D/ball imaging. Coherency and dynamics are TOTL. Clear - details are "big"/forward, but can use better separation. Super immersive. Could use more sub-bass and resolution.. Strengths: airy treble, wide/3D stage, imaging, dynamic/engaging, detailed, separation/layering. Weaknesses: lacks sub-bass. Tuning grade S, tech A. Value: Worth it

Notes: An OG EJ07 that does vocal scaling. A blast your brains out kinda set. Full, powerful, extended, VERY forward vocals, might be too much for some people. Reveals every last bit of emotion from the artist's voice. Makes the song very intimate and vulnerable. VERY genre depedent, check playlist in the video description. It's basically an RSV that scales at high volume. Super immersive, great centre-imaging (or as good as it gets in an IEM), and mid-bass quality competes with the MMK3 and others. Treble is dark, not for trebleheads or people who like air. Detail takes a hit, and stage is very close, like the artist is singing right infront of you. A truly unique experience, but again, it's gonna be a hit or miss for many people depending on their library and how loud they listen - NOT a mid-lower volume set... and it comes with a $2 pouch at $850 LOL, but hey, I mean they actually get away with it because when it hits, it HITS.. Sound: mid-centric, dark. Strengths: imaging, airy treble, detailed. Weaknesses: small stage. Tuning grade S, tech A. Value: Niche (High VOL)

Notes: Slightly warm/neutral, very well balanced, good scaling, TOTL male vocals, big staging, wait for sale. Sound: warm, neutral, balanced. Strengths: great vocals, wide/3D stage. Tuning grade S, tech A. Value: Worth it (on sale)

Notes: Airy, smooth, warm, laid-back, balanced, lush and dreamy vibes. Great for rock/metal, scales decently high. Mid-bass over sub. Not as vocal forward as Arcanis and other vocal sets. My Luna graphs very different than HBB's - wait for more reviews.. Sound: warm, balanced. Strengths: airy treble, smooth, scales with volume. Weaknesses: unit variance. Good for: rock, metal. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A+. Value: Worth it

Notes: Discontinued, but one of the best female vocals I've heard on any IEMs at higher volume. Top tier mids under $500. Spring Tips improves vocals and treble clarity. Great around the head imaging, but imaging is less layered than 07M. Treble can be dark at lower/mid volumes, but shines when cranked up. Super immersive. High volume listening recommened.. Sound: dark. Strengths: great vocals, imaging. Tuning grade S/S-, tech A. Value: Worth it

Notes: Holographic staging with an amazing midrange. Great bass texture and impact. Incredibly immersive and endgame for most. Has more sub-bass and treble air than OG doesn't scale as well.. Strengths: wide/3D stage, bass texture/slam, airy treble. Weaknesses: lacks sub-bass. Tuning grade S-, tech A+. Value: Worth it

Notes: One of the best all-rounders under $600 (v-shaped harman). Treble quality is smooth and well extended. Great low-end texture with lots of impact. Good vocals. Solid tech, and just solid in general.. Sound: v-shaped, harman. Strengths: all-rounder, smooth, bass texture/slam, great vocals, technical. Tuning grade S-, tech A+. Value: Worth it

Notes: A more resolving Davinci, literally. The Tea magic is gone :( but it's now the most refined and well-balanced. It's the most bassy one with better low-end texture, heavier notes, more details, better resolution, and the better all-rounder pick. Also bassy balanced like the Hype 4, both are just as good to me, and comes down to what I'm feeling that day. Sound: balanced, bassy. Strengths: detailed, bass texture/slam, all-rounder. Tuning grade S-, tech A+. Value: Worth it

Notes: Clean, balanced, full, natural, uppermids/vocal emphasis. Still a mid-range set, but vocals don't pop as much as the RSV I originally got, aka not as saucy. Recent unit is still a good balanced vocal set for male vocals, but not as special and very pricey, maybe on sale. This is the RSV MK1 tuning most people will get... guess I got a rare 1 of 1 lol.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: natural timbre. Tuning grade S-, tech A+. Value: Worth it (on sale)

Notes: Good but expensive. Recommended if you can find it for around $500. Direct upgrade to the AFUL Explorer. Scales great. Reminds me of the EJ07M but a bit smoother and less dynamic. Prefer it more than the OG pilgrim, but definitely not worth $400 more lol.. Strengths: scales with volume, smooth. Tuning grade S-, tech A+. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: Most balanced bass set I've heard so far without sacrificing the fun/texture/impact in the low-end. Open staging, full sounding, deep sub-bass, vocals aren't buried either. No big peaky treble, good extension. No real issues aside from the price maybe. A very unique bass experience since usually the low-end overtakes the other fr, but with the Titan you can hear everything while having that impactful/authoritative bass.. Sound: balanced. Strengths: bass texture/slam, dynamic/engaging, wide/3D stage. Weaknesses: recessed mids/vocals. Tuning grade S-, tech A+. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: Great all-rounder. Slighty airy with good sub-bass extenion. Balanced but still fun. A cleaner, airier, and less sharp/sparkly version of the Meta/Crescent - vocals pop out more. Notes: Slightly warm, full, and sparkly/crispy treble. A warmer TOP PRO with a step down in technical performance. Treble can get much on kpop/jpop/energetic tracks. Notes: Smooth listen, non-fatiguing, balanced and leans towards mids/neutral, scales good, full, natural, but lacks dynamics/transients and vocal extension. Notes: Relaxed, slightly warm-neutral tuning, a bit boring, full, could use more treble/air. Not as good as high volume (recommended listening vol).. Sound: warm, neutral. Strengths: airy treble. Tuning grade A/A+, tech A-/A. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: Clean, balanced, smooth, neutral leaning, in-offensive, good tech, everything is "fine"... a little more dynamic than Dunu 242. Sounds like the earlier units of the MEGA5ESTs. Weaknesses: recessed mids/vocals. Tuning grade S-, tech A-/A. Value: Worth it on Sale

Notes: Bassy refined v-shape sound with great low-end texture on par with odyssey and astralis - essentially a more v-shaped OG Odyssey. Vibrant, great dynamic constrast, and engaging. Notes: Slightly warm leaning with tingly treble presentation. Full, and great for male vocals, basically the Arcanis with more bass but doesn't treble is not as smooth and doesn't scale as well. Notes: If Harman wasn't boring and had a few drinks. Sound: harman. Tuning grade A+, tech A/A+. Value: Worth it

Notes: Warm and intimate signature. Vocals are very forward but lacks treble air. Needs scaling.. Sound: warm. Tuning grade A+, tech A/A+. Value: Kinda Worth it

Notes: Balanced all-rounder with good texture and detail. Good if you want a balanced listen but not very unique or different, kinda reminds me of a less shouty Harman 2019. Warm, smooth all-rounder with good accessories and build, but pricey for the performance; wait for sale. Quote: "And as for the Kinera BD005, these are a warm all rounder kind of listen, pretty smooth, you know, good accessories, good build. Pass: even brighter than the Starfield 2; better options at $50. Quote: "And then the Stellaris is even brighter than the Starfield 2's. You can get like better stuff at 50 bucks."
Pass: outdated, a bit bright, timbre not good; cheaper sets are better tuned. Quote: "So, I'm going to say a pass on the Dioko's."
Too lean, too bright, too energetic, not natural; lost to the 'Z2/Z12' planar. Quote: "dios can s a bit too lean a bit too bright a bit like too energetic not natural at all in my opinion"

Early-2023 view: great resolution and layering, close to the Hexa; treble similar in amount to the OG Olina but less even, with planar timbre. (He later calls it outdated and a pass.) Quote: "some honorable mentions would be the dyoko hexa and olena also having great resolution but just slightly warmer than Ola"

Bassy all-rounder, like a smaller, smoother EDX 300 with less resolution; recommended at ~$35. Quote: "Starting off with some newer stuff, we got the Z Cat Rhombus, and these are a bassy all-rounder."

No-brainer: best accessories under $20, bassy all-rounder; better than the Zero 2. Quote: "Similarly, the Tangzu Wan'er Z1 Base is a no-brainer. These go into top tier accessory-wise, they're the best under $20."

Pass: big 4-8 kHz hole hurts vocals and timbre; cheaper sets are better. Quote: "After those, we got the DUNU Titan S. These are going to be past tier. I mentioned this a lot. They have a huge gaping hole from 4 to 8K."

Most V-shaped and least refined of the R1/R2/R3 but cheapest; all three recommended depending on preference. Quote: "All three of these are pretty solid for the value. I'm going to say a wreck for all three of them depending"

Less treble extension and more forward upper mids than the R2; the EW100 does vocal-centric better; maybe. Quote: "But as for the RDR3s, I'm going to say this is a maybe because the treble extension is not as good, and the upper mids just pop out more."

FiiO JD1/JD10/FD11/JH13: all-rounders, not expensive, solid; bottom of rec. Quote: "Then after those, we got some feel stuff with the JD1s, the JD10s, you got the FD11s, JH13s. All of these are going to have an all-rounder sound."
Grouped with JD1/FD11/JH13: solid all-rounder for the price; bottom of rec. Quote: "I'm going to say probably at the bottom of rec like value-wise, they're not bad."
Grouped with JD1/JD10/JH13: all-rounder, slightly less V-shaped than the JD models; bottom of rec. Quote: "Main difference is that the JD stuff slightly more V-shape leaning with the FD, the JH."
Grouped with JD1/JD10/FD11: all-rounder; bottom of rec. Quote: "Then after those, we got some feel stuff with the JD1s, the JD10s, you got the FD11s, JH13s."

Wyvern variants: all-rounders with pretty plating but not competitive at ~$35; wait for $20-25. Quote: "Kinera does redeem itself with the Wren Abyss, the Remaster, the Chain, the Pros. And these are all very similar in the sound."
Wyvern variants: fine sound and nice plating but a bit expensive; wait for a sale. Quote: "but I'm going to say probably wait for these to go on sale for closer to 25, maybe 20."

TinHifi T1S/C1/C2/C3: Harman-leaning all-rounders, decent for the price; bottom of rec. Quote: "However, their other stuff like the T1S, the C1, C2, C3, these are all more Harman leaning all rounder kind of sound. They're pretty decent for the price."
Grouped with T1S/C1/C3: decent all-rounder; bottom of rec. Quote: "I would still say like a bottom of wreck. But, for the T2, DLC, Evil, whatever, those are all horrible."
Rare flat-leaning set that scales decently for $20-30; bottom of rec. Quote: "We got the Q1s and the G10s. Both of these are pretty solid. I'm going to say bottom of wreck for both of them."

Most technical of the old 'big three'; ranked above the U12T, but at ~$3K not a value pick, so get it on sale. Quote: "So I'm going to place it above the U12T, but I wouldn't say it's a value monster like it's 3K, right? So I can't really just blindly recommend it. I would say get these on sale because they are still very technical."

Grouped with the Moondrop SA8: clean, balanced; overpriced at $800, decent around $500. Quote: "Now I think these are a little bit overpriced. I think you can get these on sale for like 500. I think it's a pretty decent. But for 800, you know, I think that's a bit of a hard sell given the overall competition."

Overpriced; similar performance available for ~$500 (the IE 600 is about as technical and cheaper). Quote: "I think the IE 900 and the IE 200 are just a little bit overpriced. The 900 you can get much better stuff."

Neutral, slightly bright and 'very forgettable'; okay for a clean sound but there are better options; lost to the ZiiGaat Odyssey. Quote: "Now, the Performer 7 isn't bad. It's just very forgettable. It's a neutral slightly bright leaning set."

Balanced, clean vocal/mid-range set with good layering and stage, plus bass-boost switches. Quote: "Moving on, if you want something more balanced, something more vocal and mid-range centric, we have the KZ Zenf. Beat the T10 and EW200 on timbre and musicality; lost the final to the Tanchjim 4U, which he recommends for most people (build/QC/switches), though he personally prefers the Zenith for vocals. Quote: "Now, personally, I lean more towards the Zenith for the vocals, but I think for most people, the 4U would be the better pick."

Good single-DD: natural timbre, good layering/separation, tech like an $80-100 set at $50; cleaner EW300 but not as smooth in the treble. Quote: "overall value wise I do still recommend these even though it is KZ"

Warmer all-rounder with nicely extended treble and good sense of space; a slightly better version of the Softears Twilight. Quote: "And speaking of low one, if you want a warmer sound, give the FX17 a shot. These are a warmer allrounder. Very nicely extended in the treble."

Bright-leaning, slight V-shape, unique treble; could be a bit bright and not the best value versus Rockies/Hype 4 MK2/Horizon, but musical and enjoyable. Quote: "It focuses more on the higher frequencies, give the BGVP Solomon a shot. I think these are pretty unique, and they do have the sauce and the treble, but they could be a little bit bright."
V-shaped twin of the ND Planet: less bassy, more energetic upper mids and treble; rec if you want V-shape. Quote: "And for the price, I would give these a wreck if you want a V-shaped kind of sound."

KZ planars (PR1, PR1 Pro, PRX): great detail for under $30 but bright, sizzly and with unit variance/retune risk; PR1 Pro is the best of them; maybe. Quote: "The best one would probably be the PR1 Pros. But aside from that, I'm going to say it maybe because of like just the overall tuning and the unit variance and retunes."

Grouped with the PR1 Pro/PRX: good value but bright with unit variance; maybe. Quote: "Now, as for K's other planards, like the PR1, the P1 Pro, the PRX, all three of those are very good for the value."

Grouped with the PR1/PR1 Pro: good value but bright with unit variance; maybe. Quote: "When it comes to detail, retrieval resolution, layering, these are all great for the price, but again, I'm not sure if they're going to retune it."

Bright-leaning slight V-shape, not the smoothest; rec mainly because of case, cable and build. Quote: "I would say these are a wreck just because of the accessories, but tonality could, you know, be a little bit smoother in the overall treble and just more natural."

Very good package (case, metal build, cable) for ~$20; a bright-leaning set; the HBB Kailua sounds a step better. Quote: "so the TR and couch very good package very good case metal build quality cable is phenomenal for the price"

Bright-leaning with tuning switches; detailed but not well balanced; maybe if cheap and you like bright. Quote: "I'm going to give these a maybe if you can find these for a very good price and you like a bright leaning sound."

KZ/CCA switch models (Castor Pro, Vader Pro, Trio, Rhapsody): fun and good value but unit variance and channel imbalance with switches; maybe. Quote: "So, I'm going to say a maybe because of the QC issues. Otherwise, if you get a good unit, these are pretty top tier."
Grouped with the switchless KZ single-DD sets; top tier for value. Quote: "And they're all very similar. All like a slight V-shaped sound."
Very aggressive, bassy V-shape, not refined; better options at its price; maybe. Quote: "likewise I would also give the highest MS1 a maybe because these are a very aggressive V-shaped kind of sound"

More V-shaped and energetic, less refined treble than KZ's switchless sets; maybe. Quote: "On the other hand the CCA CRA and the CRA Plus are a bit more iffy because they are more V-shaped more energetic less refined in the treble"

Kinera house sound with forward, potentially shouty vocals and limited treble extension; sounds lower-res than the Bunny/Zero Ultima and costs more; probably a pass. Quote: "But unfortunately, I can't really recommend the Caner Celeles Waver Black Remastered Edition."
Too expensive compared with the EW300, which he prefers; probably a pass for the OG EA500 and the DSP version. Quote: "So yeah, this uh probably a pass for the OG EA500 and the DSP."

Very clean, balanced, vocal-centric set with treble extension and enough low end; bought mainly for the clean vocals and the design; good deal at ~20% off. Quote: "And then lastly, we got the Canera Verdandi. Very clean, balanced, vocal ccentric kind of set extensions there in the treble."

Beautiful plating; placed in the endgame tier, below the Monarch MK2 for him (the Kinera Loki is ranked as a better version). Quote: "next is the can verdoni these are pretty good I would say the plating alone is endgame"

Older bassy collab with a similar tuning philosophy; the HBB Arcadia is 'just a better version' with better bass texture and drivers. Quote: "I think the Arcadia has just a better version of the FHA the FHA came out a long time ago so it's not really like a fair comparison"
Slightly better treble extension than the Blon Z300; lost to the Tripowin Vivace, which he finds more refined and less peaky. Quote: "JoJo's overall slightly better and I'm going give it to the JoJo"

Bassy, warm, scales very well, good for hip-hop/rock; beat the Estrella in the semis; lost the final to the HBB Punch, which is also much cheaper. Quote: "I think the Jupiter's is good it's like a warm leaning set that skills very good"

More all-rounded and less bassy than the Empire Ears Raven but with phenomenal bass texture and sub-bass rumble; 'one of the best low end in general'. Quote: "you also have the camper CP 6226 if you want something that's more allr rounded less"

Still a solid balanced set, a bit thin, but the Blessing 3/Dusk cost the same, so 'a bit expensive' (not a 'nope'). Quote: "so because of that I'm going to say it's a bit expensive but it's not like nope right it's still decent I am"
Good in its day but overpaying at ~$200 now; definitely a no. Quote: "nowadays if you're paying 200 for this you're overpaying so definitely a no"
Still a balanced set with solid build; competes if bought used for around $100. Quote: "they still compete if you can get them used for like around 100 bucks solid build quality clean balanced"

Older ThieAudio flagships (Monarch, Excalibur, Clairvoyance) still hold up and compete though discontinued. Quote: "as for the oldest the audio stuff like the monarchs Excalibur cloran these are still competitive soundwise"
Grouped with the older Monarch and Excalibur: still competitive though discontinued. Quote: "they are discontinued but they are still very solid items if you already have them"
Unique set, a bit pricey, but still competitive for its staging; older Campfire models he would avoid. Quote: "similarly the campfire Andromeda 2020"
Better treble than the Supernova; one of the best $1K IEMs for treble, better than the Monarchs there. Quote: "same thing with the original no Helios I would actually put these at Value"
Clean mids but horrendous fit and expensive at $150; pass. Quote: "So, everything considered, this goes into pass even though it is one of the classics back in the days."
Grouped in the pass tier: too bright, treble not refined. Quote: "the original Moondrop Starfield, the Starfield 2, the Stellaris, the Aria, the Aria SE. These all go into past here."
Outdated for its price; pass tier. Quote: "The OG Starfield is just outdated for its price."
Very overpriced at $80; do not buy. Quote: "And then as for the OG Arias, these are very overpriced at $80. Do not buy these."
Slightly retuned OG Aria; also a pass. Quote: "And then the SEs are essentially a slightly retuned version of the OG Arias, also a pass."
Pass: too V-shaped, boosted on both ends. Quote: "However, unfortunately, I can't really recommend these 7Hz Five. These get a pass because it just feels too V-shaped."

Original Chu and original 7Hz Zero: game-changers back then but outclassed in 2026; probably a pass. Quote: "So, I would say probably a pass on these two unfortunately because there's just better offerings."
Hole around 4-6 kHz makes vocals incomplete; worse and pricier than the Wan'er SG Bass; skip. Quote: "So, if you don't want to waste $40 like me, I would skip these."

Sounds natural, full and smooth, but at $1,100 it is three times the Volume S / Reference price with nothing extra; he does not recommend it for most listeners. Quote: "which is why I don't really recommend these for most audio files. This is going to be a huge skip."

Overhyped: hollow vocal dip and peaky treble make timbre feel off; better, cheaper options exist. Quote: "So for me, these are a skip because I think there are better options available and I do think [music] that value-wise, they are a little bit overhyped."
Outdated; the new Dusk and cheaper sets like the Supermix 4 are better; probably skip. Quote: "I'm going to say probably skip these. There are better options available."

Original S12 and S12 Pro: bright-leaning, less refined than newer planars, cheaper alternatives exist; skip. Quote: "So, because of that, I'm going to say skip because there are better options available."
Grouped with the original S12: skip in favour of newer/cheaper planars. Quote: "Now, as for the original S12 and the S12 Pros, I think you can get cheaper stuff now in 2026."
Too safe and boring, lacks texture and detail; better sets at $20-30; skip. Quote: "You can find a lot better stuff for like 20 bucks, 30 bucks. So, because of that, I'm going to say skip"

Original Zero (Blue): the newer version is better and $50 is too much; skip. Quote: "So, because of that, I'm going to say just skip on these. You can find better stuff like the Lua Ultra, for example."

Technical, clean and sparkly but has no low end; a pass for most libraries, only for niche ones. Quote: "So, overall, a pass for most people and maybe for a certain few those, you know, that matches the library on these."
Outdated, peaky V-shape and overpriced at $130; pass unless under $50. Quote: "So yeah, I would pass on these unless again you can find these for like a steep sale for under 50"
Straight neutral, 'actually water', no bass; a pass for most people value-wise. Quote: "So, yeah, I'm going to say a pass for most people value-wise. These are not that great."

Sounds very similar to the cheaper Nora/4U/Fission; skip unless around $150. Quote: "Next, we got the Tang Fa. These are going to be a pass because you can get the Nora, you can get the Tandem for you, you can get the Fision."

Very clean vocal-centric mid-volume set with rolled-off bass; too expensive at $300 for a 2DD set; a pass for most people. Quote: "But aside from that, a very niche set and also very expensive for the price. I'm going to say this is a pass for most people."

Outdated, shouty Harman-2019-like tuning with treble roll-off; skip unless under $100. Quote: "Next, we got the Tangu and Aza collab, the Blanc Nord. These are going to be a skip for most people unless you can find these for less than 100 bucks."

Basically the same IEM as the cheaper Nora/Fission/4U; nobody should be buying the Origin. Quote: "Also, nobody should be buying the Tangent Origin or the Origin Manner. These are basically the same IM."
Much better options exist, e.g. the Tanchjim Fission at about half the price. Quote: "So, Cadens, don't buy these. There are just"

Expensive for 2BA at $170, dark and 'low res' unless played loud; maybe at $80, otherwise a pass for most people. Quote: "But for most people, this is going to be a pass because unless you're listening very loud at midv volume, these are just very low res"
Low-end scoop, neutral and expensive at $350; only for acoustic/indie libraries; a pass for most people. Quote: "So unless your library fits the Vulcan 2 to the tea, I would say this is a pass."
Peaky, shouty V-shape and too expensive at $400 given the competition; pass. Quote: "And similarly, I would also pass on the high senior cressel mainly because of two reasons."
Too expensive when the EW300 is better in his opinion; probably a pass. Quote: "So yeah, this uh probably a pass for the OG EA500 and the DSP."
Overpriced at ~$297; should be $150-200; definitely not a rec. Quote: "Yeah, Harmon's overpriced as as hell. Like this should be $200 maximum. 150 ideally. Uh yeah, definitely not a wreck."

The EW300 at the same sale price is better tuned, more technical and better built; don't get the May. Quote: "So, you know what? Actually, just scratch that. Don't get the May. Probably get the EW300."

A less V-shaped, more neutral May that sounds 'mid' and is overpriced at $100; many better options; pass. Quote: "So, I don't know if that's a fair comparison for me. This is a pass. It's a bit like just too mid for the price."

Nice plating/accessories but wonky, unrefined, peaky timbre with recessed vocals; a worse Explorer; avoid unless under $100. Quote: "and I just keep this simple and quick avoid these I don't recommend them unless you can find the Adonis new like under $100"
Grouped with the Adonis New: a less refined EW300 with harsh micro-planar treble; avoid unless ~$50-60. Quote: "I would just not really recommend the mimosas or the Adonis new"

Late treble is over-boosted, too bright and energetic even with mesh filters; avoid unless you are a treble head. Quote: "next we have the tangu wuan legend and these are just going to be a pass for me they're just a bit too bright too energetic"

Overpriced at $500 without ESTs, can sound clinical/shouty at 1-3 kHz when cranked; the EPZ P50 is cheaper and better tuned. Quote: "meteors I would say pass unless you can find these for like 200 like 250 bucks"

Tuning not very good: too much mid-bass, squished stage, and the bone-conduction driver adds jagged, unnatural peaks. Quote: "I would also avoid the pullon envil because the tuning is not very good and the bone conduction implementation is also not very good"

Very technical but shrill, fatiguing, with pressure build-up; gives him a headache and cannot really be fixed. Quote: "the Cantor is shrill it's fatiguing it has like pressure buildup it literally gives me a headache"
Definitely outdated and overpriced in his opinion; avoid. Quote: "the Kato is definitely outdated overpriced in my opinion kren is still selling them on the hangout I would avoid it"

Overpriced at $80, too dark and smooth for him despite good build; avoid for now. Quote: "however the same can be set for the kais these are just avoid these if you can for 80 bucks they are a bit overpriced"

Beyerdynamic's most legendary closed-back headphone, since 1985. Watch any BBC Radio 1 Live Lounge video on YouTube, or radio DJs in the studio: they all still use this. Truly the industry-standard closed-back. Flat, but with a bit of boost in the low and high end, so it's fun for instruments too. And if you play in a band, monitoring on this is damn excellent. Wide staging. Closed-backs are hard to make because you need an acoustic space behind the driver, and this is one of the best out there. A must; many even use it to play Valorant.

JM-1 / Meta tuning from the upper mids to the treble! Superb lower-treble performance around 4–6 kHz. Very resolving, not fatiguing at all, almost exactly the JM-1 treble roll-off. Very wide, open and spacious for the price; the treble and upper mids are very rich and resolving for the price. Highly coherent: everything feels unified, nothing sounds detached. A slightly laid-back presentation, not too forward for vocals and instruments, as if the mics were pulled back a little, giving a more distant sense of space. A really, really good IEM for just under 3 million rupiah.

Axel (impressions): bass and treble boosted; slamming bass, bright treble with lots of EST shimmer, excellent resolution and separation. "Okay, technically the Solomon has excellent resolution, details pop, and it has fantastic separation across the whole frequency spectrum from the bass, mids, and treble."
Axel: a skip; thin, sometimes artificial vocals and bright, harsh treble; bass mode adds muddiness. "So, overall, I don't like the sound of this IEM."
Precogvision lists it as a brief demo impression without a formal score (bias 3.5). "Bassy and dark sounding on the second mode. Treble is a bit choppy sounding and lacks refinement generally."

Neutral-warm, close to JM-1 "Neutral JM-1 plus a very small bass boost, or very bassy thanks to its switches. Fewer drivers than the OP24 but far better tonality: the too-shouty 4–8 kHz is safer here, though still slightly above the CrinEar Reference. From mids to lows it's very, very tidy. If you like neutral-warm at loud volume, this is nice; if you're after airy, lots of sub, a U-shaped Meta, this isn't it. Good separation; the plasticky KZ/CCA-style BA timbre is still there, but it's fairly coherent and forgivable considering the price. The air region is fairly warm."

Axel: smooth, chill, slightly warm and full with a natural, rich midrange; 4-7k can bite on energetic tracks; not the most technical. "This is how I hear the Cielo. Axel: likes it; the 5-7k dip removes treble harshness for him, with stronger sub-bass and more natural percussion. "And then, we have the Softears RSV Mark II. I like that set.
